To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the climate change projections are not as certain as often thought, (ii) there is a lot of variability in the projections and the projections are not as robust as often thought, and (iii) there is a large gap between what the scientific community thinks it knows and what society needs to know.
climate projections are needed for adaptation strategies, and that climate change adaptation is a complex and wicked problem.

(i) the development of climate information products for adaptation requires an integrated approach that involves both science and societal actors; (ii) climate information is a key element in adaptation strategies; (iii) the climate information required is not a single number, but a range of numbers; and (iv) climate information is not a single product, but a set of climate services.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of climate projections for climate change adaptation strategies in the Netherlands, with the aim to contribute to climate services for the Dutch society.

(1) the development of climate projections and climate change impact projections for the Rhine-Meuse delta region, (2) climate change adaptation information and (3) the development of new climate services for climate change adaptation.

• the development of climate projections for the Rhine-Meuse delta; • the use of climate projections in climate impact assessments; • the use, or non-use, of climate projections in decision making; and • the development and use of climate services for climate change adaptation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have learned a lot, and that we still have to learn a lot.
climate change adaptation requires a broad range of information, and this information should be available in a timely manner, at a scale that is relevant to the user.
the climate change adaptation information chain is a complex and dynamic process in which many actors are involved and in which many decisions have to be taken.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have learned a lot about how science and policy can interact in the field of climate science.
climate science is not just about climate, but about climate and society, and about climate and climate services.

we are still in the process to develop and test a new paradigm in which climate information and climate services are developed in close collaboration with users, and in which the scientific community is challenged to deliver climate information that can be used by the users in their decision-making process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the process of developing climate change information for adaptation is a complex one.

climate science can provide a wide range of products and services that can be used in adaptation strategies, but that these products and services need to be tailored to the needs of the users, and the user needs to be involved in the development process from the beginning.
the climate projections for adaptation are not just numbers.
